bar.keyboard.sensor: Keyboard: on in tablet mode, follows the switch
bar.rotation.auto: Screen rotation: automatic, follows tablet mode
bar.rotation.locked: Screen rotation: locked, turn it by hand from the controls
bar.rotation.none: Screen rotation: needs iio-sensor-proxy to follow the device
bar.rotation.stuck: Screen rotation: the sensor has stopped answering
bar.rotation.unlocked: Screen rotation: unlocked, always follows the sensor
setup.deps.how: Install them in a terminal, then come back and check again:
setup.deps.missing: Ragtop needs these from Arch's own repositories. It works without them, it just does less.
setup.finish.leave: leave Omarchy's overlays as they are
setup.finish.menu: add Ragtop's settings to your Omarchy menu, under Setup › Tablet
setup.finish.missing: Still missing: %1. Setup will finish without them. Install them whenever you like and Ragtop will pick them up.
setup.finish.restart: restart the Omarchy shell, which is when copies are picked up
setup.need.git: Cloning Omarchy's overlays, if you turn any on below.
setup.need.gobject: Noticing text fields, so the keyboard can come up by itself.
setup.need.pywayland: The on-screen keyboard. Without it no keys are sent.
setup.need.sensor: Rotation. Without it the screen won't follow the device.
setup.overlay.clipboard: Search your clipboard history by touch.
setup.overlay.image-picker: Arrows and a Select button for the theme and background pickers.
setup.overlay.lock: A keyboard of its own, to unlock without a keyboard.
setup.overlay.menu: Type to search it by touch.
setup.overlay.polkit: Type your password when something asks for it.
setup.overlays.catch: A copy is Omarchy's own code, the password prompt and lock screen included, living in your config where anything running as you can change it, and no longer taking Omarchy's updates directly (a hook re-copies them after each update). Leave them off if in doubt. They can be turned on one at a time later.
setup.overlays.why: Omarchy's menu, its pickers, its password prompt and its lock screen can't be typed into by touch as they ship. Ragtop can run patched copies of them instead.
setup.switch.either: Either way it is a setting, not a decision: Setup › Tablet › Tablet Mode changes it whenever you like. A detachable that reports a switch when its keyboard comes off will be picked up on its own.
setup.switch.none: Ragtop can notice a screen being folded back, or a keyboard coming off, by reading a tablet-mode switch, an input device the kernel exposes, like a keyboard or a mouse. This machine reports none.
setup.switch.polkit: Omarchy's password prompt will ask for your password (polkit, not sudo).
setup.switch.readable: The switch is readable already, so there is nothing to do here.
setup.switch.rule: Only root can read it here. This rule tags switch devices, tablet mode, the lid and the headphone jack, so whoever is logged in at the machine can read them. Keyboards are excluded, which is the difference between this and joining the input group.
setup.switch.skip: You can also skip it. The rule buys one thing: noticing the fold, or the detach, by itself. Rotation, the keyboard and everything else work without it. Set the mode by hand instead.
setup.switch.tablet: That is ordinary on a tablet with no keyboard, since there is nothing to fold or detach, so nothing to report. Tell Ragtop to stay in tablet mode and it will, for good.
setup.switch.what: Ragtop knows the screen has been folded back, or the keyboard taken off, by reading the tablet-mode switch, an input device the kernel exposes, like a keyboard or a mouse.
setup.title: Ragtop setup
setup.welcome.body: Ragtop makes this machine work as a tablet: the screen follows the device, an on-screen keyboard comes up when you need one, and the things that normally want a keyboard or a mouse can be done by touch.
setup.welcome.list:
• Settings rows in your Omarchy menu, written as a marked block in ~/.config/omarchy/extensions/omarchy-menu.jsonc
• Read access to the tablet-mode switch, through a udev rule that needs your password
• Patched copies of Omarchy's own overlays, if you want to type into them by touch

It will not install packages for you, and it changes nothing else.
setup.welcome.touches: Setup touches three things outside Ragtop's own folder. Each is optional, each is reversible, and nothing happens until the last step.
tools.predictions.all: English word suggestions, on any layout
tools.predictions.layout: Word suggestions, in your layout's language
tools.update.dev: A working copy: update it with git
tour.altgr.body: AltGr types the characters a layout keeps on a key's third level, like € and ß. It is sticky too.
tour.altgr.none: AltGr types the characters a layout keeps on a key's third level, like € and ß. Your layout has none, so there is no AltGr now. Switch to one that has some, and it appears.
tour.boards.body: From a phone's three rows to a full keyboard. Auto picks the widest that fits your screen, and the controls can pick one for good.
tour.done.body: Take the tour again any time from the controls, behind the gear.
tour.erase.body: Hold BackSpace, or slide left from it, to delete whole words: the label names them, and the further you slide, the more go. Slide back past where you started for none. BackSpace into a word you finished, and its suggestions come back.
tour.fn.body: On the 60% and 75% boards, Fn reaches what the board leaves out: F1 to F12 on the number row, arrows and page keys around J, Delete on Backspace. It is sticky too.
tour.fn.narrow: On the 60% and 75% boards, Fn reaches what the board leaves out: F1 to F12, arrows and page keys, Delete. Your screen is too narrow to show one here.
tour.gear.body: The gear opens the controls: key size, themes, boards, suggestions, swipe, updates, and this tour again.
tour.handle.autoShow: The keyboard also comes up by itself when you tap into a text field.
tour.handle.body: The bar along the bottom edge lowers the keyboard with a tap, and raises it again with another.
tour.letter.body: Hold a letter for its accents and the symbol in its corner, slide onto one, and let go.
tour.menu.body: Menu opens the right-click menu where you are typing, in browsers, file managers and most apps: the right click a tablet does not have. A terminal ignores it.
tour.menu.gear: Hold the gear for it: the mark in its corner says so.
tour.menu.gearOrFn: Hold the gear for it, or tap the gear with Fn on.
tour.menu.ownKey: This board has a key of its own for it.
tour.offer.body: A one-minute tour of the keyboard shows where things are and what holding a key does. It is in the controls, behind the gear, if you would rather later.
tour.space.body: Hold Space for your keyboard layouts and input methods, and slide to the one you want.
tour.space.oneLayout: Hold Space for your keyboard layouts and input methods. You have one layout now; Omarchy's keyboard settings add more.
tour.sticky.body: Tap Shift once for the next key, twice to lock it, and again to let go. Ctrl, Alt and Super work the same way, so a shortcut is one key at a time.
tour.sticky.latched: Shift is on for the next key.
tour.suggestions.body: Words appear here as you type: tap one to take it, hold one for its other forms. After a space, it offers the words likely to come next.
tour.suggestions.off: Your suggestions are off: turn them on in the controls.
tour.super.body: Super, the key every Omarchy shortcut starts with. Tap it and then a letter: Super then K lists every shortcut, Super then Space opens the launcher.
tour.swipe.body: Draw a word across the letters without lifting, and let go. It works with suggestions on.
tour.swipe.off: Your swipe typing is off: turn it on in the controls.
tour.themes.body: A theme is the keys' shape and finish. The colours always follow your Omarchy theme.
tour.welcome.body: A minute's walk around the keyboard: the keys worth knowing, and what holding them does. Tap Next to go on, or Skip tour to stop at any time.
trouble.autoshow: The keyboard is not coming up by itself
trouble.autoshow.body: The watcher that notices text fields keeps stopping. Tap the handle at the bottom to raise the keyboard by hand.
trouble.keyboard: The on-screen keyboard is not typing
trouble.keyboard.body: Ragtop's key sender keeps stopping. Check that python-pywayland is installed. Setup › Tablet › Diagnostics has the rest.
trouble.predict.body: Ragtop's word suggester keeps stopping. `ragtop words install` fetches the word list again.
trouble.rotation.body:
iio-sensor-proxy is not answering, so the screen will not follow the device. Restarting it usually clears this:
%1
trouble.switch: Tablet mode is not being noticed
trouble.switch.body: The tablet-mode switch watcher keeps stopping, so folding will not register. Setup › Tablet › Tablet Mode sets it by hand.
